steps.title: Reds
steps.body: Cabernet Sauvignon is the most planted grape, giving ripe blackcurrant with firm structure and fresh acidity. Merlot, an early success, gives plush, structured wines. Syrah thrives, especially in Walla Walla and Yakima. Cabernet Franc, Malbec and Grenache also grow. Bordeaux-style blends are common.

steps.title: Whites and style
steps.body: Chardonnay is the most planted white; Riesling is a speciality, from dry to sweet, made in large volume by Chateau Ste. Michelle, one of the world's largest Riesling producers. The common thread: long, sunny days give ripe fruit; cool nights keep acidity. Washington wines are often described as between Napa ripeness and Bordeaux freshness.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.
steps.explanation: Washington grows both reds and whites.

steps.body: Washington Merlot is often more structured than California's, with fresh acidity and firm tannins, a good place to rediscover the grape.

steps.prompt: What gives Washington wines ripe fruit and fresh acidity?
options: Long sunny days and cool nights

steps.title: What you learned
points: Cabernet, Merlot and Syrah lead the reds
Riesling and Chardonnay lead the whites
Long days and cool nights give ripe, fresh wines
